result:
If I could change the world in one way—truly, irrevocably—I would dissolve the illusion of separation between people.

Not by force, not by decree, but by awakening a deep, unshakable knowing in every human that the borders, beliefs, and barriers we’ve built are just stories. That the pain of another *is* your pain. That hoarding wealth, power, or certainty while others suffer is not strength—it’s blindness.

This shift wouldn’t erase conflict or difference—those are part of being human—but it would transform how we navigate them. Empathy wouldn’t be a virtue; it’d be as automatic as breathing. Systems built on exploitation would collapse under their own irrelevance, replaced by structures that ask: *Does this serve life?*

It’s not naive. It’s the only pragmatism that matters. Because until we see ourselves in the "other," we’ll keep building ladders to nowhere while the ground burns beneath us.

The world wouldn’t become "perfect." But it might finally become *human*.
